questions.prompt: The brave soldiers defend the high walls while the enemy approaches.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs fortēs mūrōs excelsōs dēfendunt dum hostis appropinquat.

questions.prompt: The eager student reads many books and writes letters daily.
questions.answer: Discipulus cupidus multōs librōs legit et epistulās cotīdiē scrībit.

questions.prompt: We hear the sound of the dense forest, though we see nothing.
questions.answer: Sonum dēnsae silvae audīmus, quamquam nihil vidēmus.

questions.prompt: The general leads his weary troops through the hostile fields.
questions.answer: Dux fessās cōpiās per agrōs hostīlēs dūcit.

questions.prompt: While the mother sleeps, the children carry water from the river.
questions.answer: Dum māter dormit, līberī aquam ā flūmine portant.

questions.prompt: The swift horse flees headlong from the burning stable.
questions.answer: Equus celer ex stabulō ardentī praeceps fugit.

questions.prompt: We seek the truth, but the crowd fears the powerful king.
questions.answer: Vēritātem quaerimus, sed turba rēgem potentem timet.

questions.prompt: The poet sings sweet songs while the guests drink wine.
questions.answer: Poēta dulcia carmina canit dum hospitēs vīnum bibunt.

questions.prompt: The captured city no longer resists, for the walls are falling.
questions.answer: Urbs capta iam nōn resistit, nam mūrī cadunt.

questions.prompt: The farmers cultivate the fields and the master praises their labor.
questions.answer: Agricolae agrōs colunt et dominus labōrem eōrum laudat.

questions.prompt: I take the shield and hasten toward the high tower.
questions.answer: Scūtum capiō et ad turrim excelsam properō.

questions.prompt: The wise teacher opens the book and explains difficult words.
questions.answer: Magister sapiēns librum aperit et verba difficilia explicat.

questions.prompt: You all hear the trumpets and quickly seize your weapons.
questions.answer: Tubās audītis et arma celeriter capitis.

questions.prompt: The merchants love the calm sea but dread the deep storms.
questions.answer: Mercātōrēs tranquillum mare amant sed altās tempestātēs metuunt.

questions.prompt: The maiden purifies the sacred altar while the priest prays.
questions.answer: Virgō sacram āram pūrgat dum sacerdōs ōrat.

questions.prompt: We conquer the fierce enemies and free the captives.
questions.answer: Ferōcēs hostēs vincimus et captīvōs līberāmus.

questions.prompt: The old man grows old slowly, but his mind remains keen.
questions.answer: Senex lentē cōnsenēscit, sed mēns eius ācris manet.

questions.prompt: The eager hunter throws the spear and pierces the wild boar.
questions.answer: Vēnātor cupidus hastam iacit et aprum trānsfīgit.

questions.prompt: The accomplished orator moves the citizens with powerful words.
questions.answer: Ōrātor perfectus cīvēs verbīs potentibus movet.

questions.prompt: You build a lofty temple and adorn it with gold.
questions.answer: Templum excelsum aedificās et aurō ōrnās.

questions.prompt: While sweat pours down, the runners make for the finish line.
questions.answer: Dum sūdor fluit, cursōrēs mētam petunt.

questions.prompt: The soldiers hurl their weapons and break through the dense line.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs tēla coniciunt et dēnsam aciem perrumpunt.

questions.prompt: The general prepares an ambush while the soldiers guard the camp.
questions.answer: Dux īnsidiās parat dum mīlitēs castra custōdiunt.

questions.prompt: The philosopher praises restraint and despises useless riches.
questions.answer: Philosophus continentiam laudat et inānēs dīvitiās contemnit.

questions.prompt: We hear the citizens' clamor and hasten toward the citadel.
questions.answer: Cīvium clāmōrem audīmus et ad arcem contendimus.

questions.prompt: You turn pale whenever you catch sight of the dreadful monster.
questions.answer: Pallēs cum horrendum mōnstrum vidēs.

questions.prompt: The orator pours forth long speeches before the assembled people.
questions.answer: Ōrātor longās ōrātiōnēs ante populum congregātum diffundit.

questions.prompt: The little boy fears the wolf and flees into the woods.
questions.answer: Parvus puer lupum timet et in silvās fugit.

questions.prompt: We build a bridge while the swift river flows down from the mountains.
questions.answer: Pontem aedificāmus dum rapidus amnis dē montibus dēfluit.

questions.prompt: You (pl.) rule the province with justice and restrain the greedy.
questions.answer: Prōvinciam cum iūstitiā regitis et avārōs coercētis.

questions.prompt: The weary traveler, about to depart, seeks a brief rest.
questions.answer: Fessus viātor itūrus brevem quiētem petit.

questions.prompt: The queen adorns the golden helmet with precious gems.
questions.answer: Rēgīna auream galeam pretiōsīs gemmīs ōrnat.

questions.prompt: We count the stars while the shepherd leads his flock home.
questions.answer: Stēllās ēnumerāmus dum pāstor gregem domum dūcit.

questions.prompt: You grieve because the war drags on and the allies withdraw.
questions.answer: Dolēs quod bellum diū manet et sociī dēcēdunt.

questions.prompt: The wise judge hears the case and condemns the guilty man.
questions.answer: Sapiēns iūdex causam audit et reum damnat.

questions.prompt: The sailors dread the deep sea and the raging winds.
questions.answer: Nautae altum mare et saevōs ventōs metuunt.

questions.prompt: We greet our friends who are returning from the long journey.
questions.answer: Amīcōs ex longō itinere reversōs salūtāmus.

questions.prompt: You (pl.) open the gates and receive the weary guests.
questions.answer: Portās aperītis et fessōs hospitēs accipitis.

questions.prompt: The farmer plows the field while the sun rises over the hills.
questions.answer: Agricola agrum arat dum sōl super collēs surgit.

questions.prompt: The teacher explains the difficult book to the eager students.
questions.answer: Magister difficilem librum studiōsīs discipulīs explicat.

questions.prompt: We guard the sacred fire and feed the flame through the night.
questions.answer: Sacrum ignem custōdīmus et per noctem flammam alimus.

questions.prompt: You know many things, but you conceal the truth from the king.
questions.answer: Multa scīs sed vērum ā rēge cēlās.

questions.prompt: The general leads the legions across the wide plain toward the city.
questions.answer: Dux legiōnēs per lātam plānitiem ad urbem dūcit.

questions.prompt: The merchant sells rare wares and gathers great wealth.
questions.answer: Mercātor rāra mercimōnia vendit et magnās dīvitiās colligit.

questions.prompt: We warn the young men, but they scorn our counsel.
questions.answer: Iuvenēs monēmus, sed cōnsilium nostrum spernunt.

questions.prompt: You (pl.) hurl spears at the enemy and shatter their battle line.
questions.answer: Tēla in hostēs iacitis et aciem frangitis.

questions.prompt: When he had said this in a loud voice, he threw himself from the ship and began to carry the eagle against the enemy.
questions.answer: Hoc cum vōce māgnā dīxisset, sē ex nāvī prōiēcit atque in hostēs aquilam ferre coepit.

questions.prompt: A multitude of books distracts; and so, since you cannot read as much as you have, it is enough to have as much as you may read.
questions.answer: Distringit librōrum multitūdō; itaque cum legere nōn possīs quantum habuerīs, satis est habēre quantum lēgās.

questions.prompt: I will easily induce the same men to escort you all the way to the gates as you leave behind these things which you have long been eager to lay waste.
questions.answer: Eōsdem facile addūcam, ut tē haec quae vastāre iam prīdem studēs relinquentem, usque ad portās prōsequantur.

questions.prompt: Nor was there anyone at all who did not think that the outcome of all his fortunes rested on the chance of that day.
questions.answer: Neque erat quisquam omnium quīn in eius diēī cāsū suārum omnium fortūnārum ēventum cōnsistere existimāret.

questions.prompt: Nor could any wind blow without their having a favorable course in some quarter.
questions.answer: Neque ūllus flāre ventus poterat quīn aliquā ex parte secundum cursum habērent.

questions.prompt: He reached the enemy's camp before the Germans could perceive what was being done.
questions.answer: Prius ad hostium castra pervēnit quam quid agerētur Germānī sentīre possent.

questions.prompt: How often did daylight surprise him having set about writing something in the night, how often did night overtake him when he had begun in the morning!
questions.answer: Quotiēns illum lūx noctū aliquid dēscrībere ingressum, quotiēns nox oppressit, cum māne coepisset!

questions.prompt: So it comes about that those men talk about their master — men who are not permitted to speak in the master's presence.
questions.answer: Sīc fit: ut istī dē dominō loquantur — quibus cōram dominō loquī nōn licet.

questions.prompt: But you will forgive me; for I have been carried away by my enthusiasm for country matters, and old age is by nature rather talkative — so that I may not seem to be clearing it of every fault.
questions.answer: Ignōscētis autem; nam et studiō rūsticārum rērum prōvectus sum, et senectūs est nātūra loquācior — nē ab omnibus eam vitiīs videar vindicāre.

questions.prompt: Many were found of such a character as to be ready to give their lives for their country.
questions.answer: Inventī multī sunt quī vītam prōfundere prō patriā parātī essent.

questions.prompt: Themistocles used to walk about at night because he could not sleep.
questions.answer: Noctū ambulābat Themistoclēs quod somnum capere nōn posset.

questions.prompt: When he understood that all agreed he appointed the next day for the battle.
questions.answer: Ubi omnīs idem sentīre intellēxit, posterum diem pūgnae cōnstituit.

questions.prompt: They were preparing to do this by night, when the women suddenly ran out into the streets.
questions.answer: Hōc facere noctū apparābant, cum mātrēs familiae repente in pūblicum prōcurrērunt.

questions.prompt: I shall not hesitate to take pains to see you, when I can do it conveniently.
questions.answer: Nōn dubitābō dare operam ut tē videam, cum id satis commodē facere poterō.

questions.prompt: Since solitude is full of treachery and fear, reason itself prompts us to contract friendships.
questions.answer: Cum sōlitūdō īnsidiārum et metūs plēna sit, ratiō ipsa monet amīcitiās comparāre.

questions.prompt: And that they did not refuse to fight.
questions.answer: Neque recūsāre quīn armīs contendant.
